## Correction from the `domain:ui` seat — this card was ruled two hours ago and I kept reporting it as awaiting the maintainer

Session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`. No label change (`pm:queue` is correct), no claim yet — recording an error of mine so the card's status is not misread again.

**This card was RULED at 2026-08-29T01:46:28Z** (maintainer, live director session batch #3, verbatim 「同意」), adopting option B in its only accepted shape: the precise `sideEffects` **array plus the companion gate, as one unit**, with a bare array explicitly refused. The ruling moved it to `pm:queue` and named it the implementation carrier.

**I went on listing it as "awaiting the maintainer" in round reports after that** — for roughly two hours — because I was reading a hand-maintained list in my seat post that was written the previous evening, before the ruling existed. The card was dispatchable that whole time, and it is the highest-value item on this lane's board: ~242.6 KB off the console eager closure, headroom ~0.9% → ~8%.

⚠️ **This is the second card from that same ruling batch I mis-filed the same way.** #6237 was ruled in the same batch, at the same minute, and I dispatched it against a stale note too — with an order that contradicted its ruling. Two errors, one cause: **a hand-copied decision list that rots between rounds and then gets trusted over the labels.**

⇒ The fix is already applied: this lane's decision box is now **derived from `label:needs-user-decision`** rather than restated, and the hand list is being removed from the seat post. Derived from labels just now, the real box for `domain:ui` holds two cards — neither of them this one.

### What happens next on this card

It is **reserved as the next dispatch** for this lane. In-flight is at the standing cap of 5 (`priority:p1` does not carry the p0 exemption that allows exceeding it), so it goes out as soon as a slot frees rather than displacing work already running.

The dispatch order will carry the ruling verbatim, and in particular these three constraints, which are the parts most easily lost:

1. **Array and gate are one unit.** ⛔ A bare array without the gate is refused by the ruling — an incomplete array fails silently in consumers' bundles with zero witnesses, the same failure mode that closed option C by measurement.
2. **The enumeration is re-derived mechanically, never copied.** The ruling says the implementing PR re-derives it; the "10 modules" figure is today's measurement, not an input to paste.
3. **The `MAX_EAGER_CLOSURE_GZIP_BYTES` downward re-baseline the gate demands at exit 2 is part of the ruled work**, not a follow-up.

Plus the controls the ruling names: the three at-risk SDUI registrations (`mcp:connect-agent`, `cloud:onboarding-next`, `cloud:ai-model-status`) pinned present at ≥1 chunk each.

The ruled shape shipped **as one unit**: a precise 23-entry `sideEffects` array (entry forms including `./src/styles.css`, plus the ten registering modules in **both** `src` and `dist` spellings), `check-side-effects-array.mjs` re-deriving the enumeration from module bodies, `check-sdui-registration-pins.mjs` weighing the built console, and the downward re-baseline (`MAX_EAGER_CLOSURE_GZIP_BYTES` 3,345,000 → 3,300,000). Both gates wired into CI.

## ⚠️⚠️ For the maintainer: the figure this card was ruled on does not survive measurement

**This is an informational correction, not a request to re-decide.** The ruled work is delivered, measured and gated, and it stands on its own.

| | ruled expectation | measured on `f905b0753` |
|---|---|---|
| eager-closure reduction | **~242.6 KB** | **55.3 KiB** (−56,668 gz, 1.71%) |
| headroom | **~0.9% → ~8%** | **1.04% → 1.41%** |

**Where the 242.6 KB came from, re-measured rather than guessed:** it is `sideEffects: false`'s number. The developer reproduced `false` on today's tree — 3,067,760 gz, −242,912 B — and it drops **FOUR** live registrations to zero chunks: the three ruled controls **plus `cloud-connection:panel`**, one more than this card recorded. So the disproof of `false` is now stronger than when it was written.

**Why the precise array cannot reach that number:** the 187 KiB between the two **is** the closure the ten registering modules anchor. `metadata-admin` alone is **168.6 KiB**, held eager because `views/metadata-admin/index.ts` registers at module top level. Releasing it means dropping registrations — which is the option measurement already closed.

⇒ **The near-zero-headroom condition (#6631) is improved, not ended.** This card was ranked highest-value on the premise that it would end it. That premise was `false`'s, and `false` is disproven.

⭐ The lane lesson, recorded: **a card's priority rationale expires too.** When a card cites a benefit figure, ask which option it was measured under.

**Seat disposition on the developer's open question: option A**, and it stays out of the decision box because it is a ranking call, not a ruling. This PR lands as the ruled work; **#6681** (~194 KiB, `metadata-admin` the bulk) is re-ranked as the card that would actually end the condition, and this PR is its **prerequisite, not its substitute**. Option C — giving `views/metadata-admin/index.ts` an explicit registration API — is the honest long-term direction, overlaps #6681, and should be decided **there** on its own measurement rather than folded back into a card already ruled.

---

## Verification

⭐ **The enumeration was not tuned to the expected answer.** The mechanical derivation returned **exactly 10**, agreeing with the card's "measured at 10 today" as an **independent** derivation. My dispatch order warned that adjusting the mechanism until it returned 10 would be manufacturing the answer; it did not have to be adjusted.

⛔ **A miscount of mine, corrected before it reached anyone:** I read the array as "11 entries ≠ the ruled 10" from a raw grep. Wrong — the array is 23 entries: **entry forms plus ten modules in two spellings each**. My count conflated the two categories. Recorded because I nearly reported my own crude count as a finding.

**Ablations, both from the committed tree, mutations proven on disk by anchored counts and a moved blob hash, restores proven by hash equality and an empty `git diff HEAD`:**

- **(A) `sideEffects: false`** → pins exit 2, budget exit 2, closure 3,067,760 gz, and the four registrations at 0 chunks. ⭐ The static gate's **exit 0** is **reported rather than glossed**: `false` takes the package out of that gate's population *by construction*, and the false direction belongs to `side-effects-declaration-consistency.test.ts`. Refusing to claim a gate caught something it structurally cannot is the right instinct.
- **(B) the array minus ONE control module** (both spellings) → static gate exit 1 **naming both missing spellings**, and the resulting dist reads `mcp:connect-agent` at 0 chunks **while the other four controls stay at 1**. Surgical: exactly the excluded module, nothing else.

**Gate discrimination**: 23 cases for the array gate — missing registrar, missing published spelling, missing entry form, stale name, name existing nowhere, unrecognised top-level effect, a glob, an unresolved specifier, a non-round-tripping spelling map, a registrar reachable only through a shakeable module, an empty population — **each with its passing partner**. 11 for the pins gate, including ⭐ a case that reds on **a matcher that cannot miss**.

⭐ **A side effect the gate demanded, reported rather than absorbed:** the console build's `missing` verdict named `RecordFormPage` and `ReportView` as no longer eager (their #6680 chunk co-tenants became shakeable), so both lines left `DECLARED_LAZY_VIEWS_STILL_EAGER`. That removes an instance of #6680 **without closing that card**.

**NOT MEASURED, declared as such:** `check:readme-exports` exits 1 in an unbuilt worktree with 379 findings across packages this PR does not touch — the unbuilt-tree prerequisite, not a red. Repo-scoped claims (full test farm, `turbo run lint`, `turbo run type-check`) named as unverified until CI speaks.

## Follow-up filed

**#6736** — `check-changeset-presence.mjs` guards only `PKG/src/**`, so a **published-contract change in `package.json`** (`sideEffects`, `exports`, `files`, `main`, `types`, `peerDependencies`) is owed no changeset and **can ship unrecorded**. This PR is the live instance: the gate said no changeset was owed, and one shipped anyway. ⭐ Found by a developer noticing that its own PR was not required to declare itself.

## Correction to my ACCEPT — this card's body did NOT conflate the two figures; its title did

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`. Closure confirmed: `closed_by_pull_requests` → PR #6735, MERGED. Correcting my own framing on the record, because it was unfair to this card's author.

My ACCEPT said the ruling's expected effect "does not re-verify" and read as though the card had attributed `sideEffects: false`'s benefit to option B. **It did not.** The body states it outright, in a labelled table:

| | console eager closure (gzip) | headroom |
|---|---|---|
| today | 3237.0 KB | 29.6 KB |
| PR #6682 (shipped) | 3231.7 KB | 34.9 KB |
| **with `"sideEffects": false`** | **2994.4 KB** | **272.2 KB** |

— and then, in the author's own words: *"The 242.6 KB above is what `false` buys, and part of what it buys is **deleting working features**."* Option C is marked closed by measurement on the same page.

⇒ **The measurement was correctly scoped where it was made.** What went wrong is narrower and more interesting:

⭐ **The figure escaped from a qualified body into an unqualified title** — *"Measured at 242.6 KB gzipped — 8x today's console headroom"* — and into the urgency argument, *"the only measured lever that would end that condition instead of managing it."* Both sentences are about `false`. Neither says so. From there the number reached the ruling, which adopted **option B** while citing **option C's** benefit.

The substantive finding stands and is unchanged: **option B delivers 55.3 KiB, headroom 1.04% → 1.41%**, and **#6631's near-zero-headroom condition is improved, not ended**. #6681 remains the lever that would end it. But the error was not in this card's measurement, and my ACCEPT should not have implied it was.

⇒ The lane lesson, restated more precisely: **a card's title and its urgency framing are load-bearing, and they can carry a number the body has correctly qualified.** A ruling reads the headline. When a benefit figure appears in a title, it should name the option it was measured under.

⚠️ For whoever prices **#6681** next: its ~194 KiB figure should be re-checked the same way — under which option was it measured, and does it survive the shape that would actually be implemented?
